data.hypothesis: The previously measured binomial-weighted sum reduced mean latency from 0.39008 s to 0.16014 s but retained 64 powf calls per input element. Generating the required terminal values from one powf(u, -64) followed by 63 multiplications by u*u may reduce math-library work further. This may alter rounding, so correctness and latency must be measured rather than assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: This experiment retains the weighted-sum algorithm but changes terminal power generation; repeat all correctness cases and numerical edge cases without relaxing tolerance.
memory_lessons.claim: The weighted-sum candidate was valid on all 8 reported cases, with mean latency 0.1601446 s versus the 0.3900794 s baseline; its reported maximum absolute errors were up to 3.8147e-05.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this variant against the same baseline and weighted-sum candidate, and inspect any correctness failures before attempting further changes.

data.notes: This is a distinct follow-up to the measured weighted-sum candidate: it preserves indices j=0..63, exponents 2*j-64, the 63-trial weights, and 63 discount factors, while changing only terminal-power generation. Prior official means were 0.3900794 s for baseline and 0.1601446 s for the weighted-sum candidate. This variant has not been measured; latency and correctness, including numerical edge cases, are pending controller evaluation.
transformations: Replaced 64 independent terminal powf evaluations per input element with one powf(u, -64) and sequential multiplication by u*u to generate the 64 payoff powers.
Retained the binomial-weighted sum over terminal indices 0..63, corresponding to 63 effective updates, and retained exactly 63 discount factors.
